classification.difficultyReason: Derives the sine rule by expressing the same triangle area using three opposite side–angle pairs.

content.prompt:
In this exercise we’ll give an alternative proof of the sine rule. Use the formula for the area of a triangle introduced in the previous section to prove that
$$\frac{2}{abc}\operatorname{area}(\triangle ABC)=\frac{\sin A}{a}=\frac{\sin B}{b}=\frac{\sin C}{c}.$$

answer.short:
$$\frac{2}{abc}\operatorname{area}(\triangle ABC)=\frac{\sin A}{a}=\frac{\sin B}{b}=\frac{\sin C}{c}.$$

Apply the area rule at each vertex and divide each expression by $\frac{abc}{2}$.
answer.worked:
Applying the area rule at each vertex gives
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{area}(\triangle ABC)&=\frac12bc\sin A\\\operatorname{area}(\triangle ABC)&=\frac12ca\sin B\\\operatorname{area}(\triangle ABC)&=\frac12ab\sin C.
\end{align*}$$
Multiplying each expression by $\dfrac{2}{abc}$ gives
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2}{abc}\operatorname{area}(\triangle ABC)&=\frac{\sin A}{a}\\\frac{2}{abc}\operatorname{area}(\triangle ABC)&=\frac{\sin B}{b}\\\frac{2}{abc}\operatorname{area}(\triangle ABC)&=\frac{\sin C}{c}.
\end{align*}$$
Thus all four expressions are equal, as required.
